title: Satellite Edge: Minimal Deployment and Bandwidth-Aware Upgrade Playbook
author: Elena Kim
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes a reproducible, minimal-footprint deployment pattern for satellite edge sites (retail kiosks, regional branches, offline customer premises) and a safe, bandwidth-aware upgrade and rollback procedure for model artifacts and runtime packages. It is intended for operator teams supporting small-footprint private deployments where network bandwidth is constrained, connectivity is intermittent, and forensic preservation is required for rollbacks and compliance evidence.

Who should read this:
- Field operators performing initial installs and upgrades
- Platform engineers building packaging and artifact flows for airgapped or low-bandwidth sites
- SREs and security engineers who own rollback and evidence-preservation requirements

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Redwood Private edge appliances and VPC-branch satellite deployments with <100 Mbps sustained bandwidth or intermittent WAN connectivity.
- Assumes Kubernetes-based runtime with audited artifact signing (cosign/Notary) and a lightweight agent (satellite-agent) that orchestrates local model placement and KV-cache warmstart.
- Not a replacement for full-site private-deploy runbooks; this is the minimal, operator-facing path for small sites.

Goals:
- Minimize on-site footprint (RAM, disk, power) while preserving SLOs for short interactive sessions (95th percentile latency target: 250–500 ms depending on model size).
- Ensure upgrades are bandwidth-aware and can be staged using delta deltas or container-layer diffing to reduce transfer size.
- Provide deterministic rollback with preserved signed artifacts and an evidence bundle for audits.

High-level architecture (text diagram):
- Control plane (Redwood hosted or dedicated control plane) 
  -> Artifact distribution service (edge-relay) with delta bundles and resume-capable transfer
  -> Operator-facing coordination console (console routes, per-site policies)
- Satellite site: small k8s node(s) running runtime, satellite-agent, local KV-cache, and optional tiny object store for model fragments.

Prerequisites checklist (operator must verify before install):
1) Hardware: CPU cores >=4, RAM >=32 GiB, NVMe >=256 GiB or network-backed model cache, TPM 2.0 for attestation (preferred).
2) Network: Egress to artifact relay allowed via TLS; site firewall allows outbound port 443 and SSH for operator access.
3) Keys & signing: Customer KMS or Redwood-managed signing key registered; cosign key bundle stored in control plane.
4) Operator credentials: Operator service account and service token with limited scope (artifact-download, health-report).
5) Capacity plan: Acceptable SLO thresholds and burst policy set in site manifest.

Minimum runtime config (example table):
| Component | Minimum | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| kube node count | 1 | Single-node tolerant if state snapshots are stored remotely |
| disk partition for model cache | 100 GiB | Prefer NVMe; can use encrypted LVM |
| satellite-agent memory | 256 MiB | Lightweight; controls transfers and KV warmstart |
| local object store | 20 GiB | Optional; holds delta fragments for resume transfers |

Operator deployment steps (initial install):
1) Preflight: run preflight script on operator laptop against target site: 
   ./satellite-preflight.sh --site-id S001 --verify-hw --verify-network
   - Exit codes: 0 = pass, 1 = warnings, 2 = failures. Address any failures.
2) Bootstrap attestation: enroll TPM -> request attestation token via control plane: 
   redwoodctl enroll --site S001 --attest --output enroll-token.json
3) Provision minimal runtime: apply site manifest (YAML snippet):
   apiVersion: redwood/v1
   kind: SiteManifest
   metadata:
     name: satellite-s001
   spec:
     runmode: minimal
     modelCacheSizeGiB: 100
     signedArtifactPolicy: cosign
4) Start satellite-agent: docker run --rm -e ENROLL_TOKEN=@enroll-token.json redwood/satellite-agent:v1.4.
5) Smoke test: curl -sS https://site-local:8443/healthz && redwoodctl site-status --site S001

Bandwidth-aware upgrade strategy:
- Use delta bundles: control plane builds delta bundles between model versions (e.g., v1.12 -> v1.13) and produces compressed fragment sets. The satellite-agent supports resume and parallel chunked downloads with backoff tuned to measured WAN RTT.
- Throttle policy: default to 10% of available bandwidth or 10 Mbps (whichever is smaller) during business hours; full bandwidth use allowed in maintenance windows.

Upgrade workflow (safe staged upgrade):
1) Prepare stage: create signed artifact and delta bundle in control plane. Patch manifest with target version and schedule window.
2) Canary stage (local): schedule a local canary traffic slice (5% traffic or synthetic tests) routed to canary runtime instance.
3) Transfer stage: satellite-agent pulls delta bundle with resume capability. Transfer command example: 
   redwoodctl transfer --site S001 --artifact v1.13 --policy delta --max-rate 5Mbps --resume
4) Apply & warmstart: apply new model files to model cache; warmstart KV-cache using last-known prefixes up to safe token cutover.
5) Validation: run acceptance test set (see Acceptance tests section). If all pass, promote; otherwise trigger rollback.

Rollback and forensic evidence preservation:
- Rollback is treated as a first-class operation with an evidence bundle. Every upgrade operation produces an immutable evidence bundle consisting of:
  - signed artifact manifests (cosign signatures)
  - site telemetry snapshot (pre-upgrade health, disk checksums)
  - transfer logs with checksums and timestamps
- Rollback command (operator): 
  redwoodctl rollback --site S001 --to-version v1.12 --preserve-evidence /tmp/evidence-20260302.tar.gz
- Rollback steps: stop accepting new sessions on failed instance, restore previous model files by applying reverse delta, verify checksums, restart services, run acceptance tests, and upload evidence bundle to control plane for storage and audit.

Acceptance tests (automated):
- End-to-end latency test: 100 synthetic queries (model small), 95th percentile < 500 ms.
- Sanity outputs: deterministic test prompts return expected token prefixes (baseline prompt set stored in control plane).
- KV-cache consistency check: verify that restored state has consistent SSE checksums across tile boundaries.
- Disk integrity: model file checksums must match signatures in cosign bundle.

Operator runbook (quick actions):
- Connectivity degraded during transfer: pause transfer, capture partial fragment list, resume after network recovers.
- Failed canary: immediately roll back canary instance, escalate via operator channel #satellite-ops, and set site to maintenance.
- Silent drift detected (latency/regression): snapshot environment, run regression harness against baseline prompt set, and if regression confirmed, freeze rollout and initiate rollback.

Bandwidth mitigation techniques (practical tips):
- Prefer delta bundles and layer diffs over full model pushes.
- Use XOR-sparse patching for model shards to reduce transfer sizes for small quant tweaks.
- Enable compression at transport and optionally use rsync-like chunking over HTTP with SHA-256 chunk checks.
- Schedule large transfers during local night windows and provide an operator override for emergency fast-transfer.

Configuration examples (YAML snippet for a site policy):
sitePolicy:
  maxBandwidthMbps: 10
  maintenanceWindow: 02:00-04:00
  canaryPercent: 5
  deltaPolicy: enabled
  preserveEvidence: true

Operational ownership matrix:
- Field operator: executes preflight, bootstrapping, transfer execution, and rollback commands.
- Platform engineering: builds delta bundles, maintains control-plane artifact relay, and configures canary traffic routing.
- Security: signs artifacts and validates evidence bundles for compliance requests.

Post-upgrade checklist (must complete within 24 hours):
1) Confirm acceptance tests green and record results in evidence bundle.
2) Verify cosign signatures of deployed artifacts.
3) Upload transfer logs and checksums to control plane.
4) Update site manifest with new model version and operator notes.
5) Run nightly synthetic tests for 72 hours; escalate on any deviation.

Troubleshooting guide (common failure modes):
- Partial transfer corruption: compare chunk checksums against control plane, re-request missing fragments using --resume.
- KV-cache warmstart fails: fallback to cold-start path with a temporary SLO relaxation policy for 1 hour and notify customer.
- Disk space pressure: evict least-recently-used model shards according to eviction policy and pause transfers until space restored.

Audit and compliance notes:
- Evidence bundle retention: default 365 days, configurable per customer in the site manifest.
- All operator actions are logged and require multi-signer confirmation for rollback on regulated sites.

Related pages and references:
- See reference architectures for local model fanout and minimal runtime footprint for additional topology options.
- Packaging guide for signed images and offline artifact signing.

Appendix A — Example cosign verification command:
cosign verify --key kms://projects/redwood/keys/satellite-signer artifact.tar.gz

Appendix B — Minimal acceptance test manifest (JSON snippet):
{
  "tests": [
    {
      "name": "latency-95p",
      "queries": 100,
      "threshold_ms": 500
    },
    {
      "name": "sanity-prefix",
      "baseline_set_id": "satellite-baseline-2026"
    }
  ]
}

Contact and escalation:
- Primary on-call: #satellite-ops Slack channel (pager linked)
- Escalation: Satellite on-call -> Platform lead -> Security for evidence-preservation issues

End of document.
